senses.gloss: यष्टव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be worshipped, &c.

यष्टव्य यष्टव्य, यष्टृ. See p. 804,
col. 2.

1. यष्टि, इस्, f. (for 2. यष्टि see s.v.), sacrificing,
(perhaps incorrect for 3. इष्टि.)

यष्टि 2. यष्टि, इस्, f. (rarely m.), or यष्टी,
f. (probably fr. rt. यम्; for 1. यष्टि see p. 804,
col. 2), a staff, stick, wand; a staff armed with iron,
mace, club; a pole, column, pillar; a perch; a stem, sup-
port; a palisade; a flag-staff [cf. ध्वज-य्˚]; a stalk,
stem, blade; a reed; a branch; the arm (= भुज-
दण्ड); anything thin or slender (e. g. अङ्ग-
यष्टि, a slender or delicate form; असि-यष्टि, a
sword-blade; cf. गात्र-य्˚, शरीर-य्˚, भुज-य्˚); a
string, thread (= तन्तु), string of pearls, necklace
[cf. हार-य्˚]; a particular kind of pearl necklace;
liquorice (= यष्टी-मधुक, मधुका); sugar-
cane (= मधु-यष्टि); Clerodendrum Siphonan-
thus (= भार्गी); any creeping plant.
—यष्टि-
गृह, अम्, n., N. of a district.
—यष्टि-ग्रह,
अस्, आ, अम्, carrying a stick or staff; (अस्), m. a club-
bearer, mace-bearer, staff-bearer.
—यष्टि-निवास,
अस्, m. a pole serving as a perch (for peacocks,
Raghu-v. XVI. 14); a pigeon-house standing on
upright poles; [cf. वास-यष्टि.]
—यष्टि-प्राण,
अस्, आ, अम्, one whose strength or power is as slender
as a stalk or reed, powerless or feeble as a reed
(= यष्टिर् वेणु-दण्ड एव प्राणः शक्तिर् यस्य
सः); out of breath.
—यष्टि-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्,
having a stick or staff, furnished with a flag-staff.
—यष्टि-मधु, उ, n. or यष्टि-मधुका, f.
[]
liquorice.
—यष्टि-यन्त्र, अम्, n. a particular
astronomical instrument.
—यष्टी-पुष्प, अस्, m.,
N. of a plant, Putranjiva Roxburghii; [cf. पुत्र-
जीव.]
—यष्टी-मधु, उ, or यष्टी-मधुक,
अम्, n. = यष्टि-मधु.
—यष्ट्य्-आघात, अस्, m.
a blow with a stick, a cudgeling, beating.
—यष्ट्य्-
आह्व or यष्ट्य्-आह्वय, अस्, m. liquorice.
यष्टी. See under 2. यष्टि, p. 812, col. 3.

यष्टु-काम, अस्, आ, अम्, desiring to worship,
wishing or intending to sacrifice.

यष्टृ, टा, ट्री, टृ, one who worships or sacri-
fices, a worshipper, sacrificer (= यजमान).
यश यश. See col. 3.

यश at the end of a comp. = यशस्, cf. अति-य्˚;
(अम्), n., N. of a Sāman.

यास यास, अस्, m. = यवास, Alhagi Mau-
rorum; (आ), f. a species of thrush, Turdus Salica.

यशद यशद, अम्, n. a species of mineral
(commonly called दस्ता, which according to some
is zinc or pewter).

यशस् यशस्, अस्, n. (in Uṇādi-s. IV. 190.
said to be fr. rt. 1. अश्; according to some for ori-
ginal दशस् = Lat. decus, fr. a lost rt. दश्), beautiful
or handsome appearance, beauty, splendor, magnifi-
cence, worth, excellence (Ved.); honour, glory,
praise, renown, fame, reputation, distinction, cele-
brity; Fame (personified as the son of Kāma and
Rati or of Dharma and Kīrtti); an object of honour
or respect, a person of respectability; favour, parti-
ality (Ved.); = उदक, water (Ved.); अन्न, food
(Ved.); = धन, wealth (Ved.); N. of a Sāman;
(आस्), m. a proper N.; (आस्, आस्, अस्), Ved. beautiful,
handsome, splendid, resplendent; worthy, excellent;
renowned, honoured, respected, venerated; pleasant,
pleasing, agreeable, estimable; [cf. Gr. δοκ-έ-ω,
δόξα, δόγμα, δοκεύω, διδάσκω, δάκτυλος; Lat.
dec-et, decus, dignu-s, doceo; probably Angl. Sax.
ta, tah; Old Germ. zeha.]
—यशः-कर्ण, अस्, m.,
N. of a king.
—यशः-काय, अस्, m. a body consisting
of fame or glory, i. e. glory, reputation.
—यशः-
केतु, उस्, m., N. of various kings.
—यशः-पटह,
अस्, m. a drum, a double drum.
—यशः-पाल, अस्,
m., N. of a king.
—यशः-प्रख्यापन, अम्, n.
spreading abroad or proclaiming the glory (of any
one).
—यशः-शरीर, अम्, n. = यशः-काय above.
—यशः-शेष, अस्, आ, अम्, having nothing left but
glory or fame, i. e. dead; (अस्), m. death, dying.
—यशश्-चन्द्र, अस्, m., N. of a king.
—यशस्-
कर, अस्, ई, अम्, causing renown, conferring fame
or distinction, famous, glorious; (अस्), m., N. of
various men.
—यशस्कर-स्वामिन्, N. of a temple
founded by a certain Yaśas-kara.
—यशस्-काम, अस्,
आ, अम्, honour-loving, desirous or eager for fame,
ambitious.
—यशस्-काम्य, Nom. P. -काम्यति,
&c., to desire honour or fame, be eager for renown.
—यशस्-काम्यत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, desiring fame, de-
sirous of glory.
—यशस्-कृत्, त्, त्, त्, causing honour,
conferring dignity or renown.
—यशस्-तम, अस्,
आ, अम्, Ved. most renowned or resplendent.
—य-
शस्-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, possessing honour or glory,
full of honour, honourable, glorious, famous; pleasant,
pleasing, excellent, handsome; agreeable, estimable;
(अती), f., N. of a woman.
—यशस्वि-तम, अस्, आ,
अम्, most famous or renowned.
—यशस्-विन्, ई, इनी,
इ, possessing honour or glory, renowned, famous, cele-
brated, glorious; excellent, handsome; (इनी), f. epithet
of a particular artery; N. of several plants, wild cotton
(= वन-कार्पासी, यव-तिक्ता, महा-ज्योतिष्मती);
N. of one of the Mātṛs attending on Skanda.
—यशो-
गोपि, इस्, m., N. of a commentator on the Śrauta-
sūtras of Kātyāyana.
—यशो-घ्न, अस्, ई, अम्, de-
stroying the appearance or beauty (Ved.); destroying
fame or reputation.
—यशो-द, अस्, आ, अम्, glory-
giving, bestowing distinction, conferring fame or
renown; (अस्), m. quicksilver; (आ), f., N. of the
wife of the cowherd Nanda, (she resided at Go-kula,
and was the foster-mother of Kṛṣṇa, who immedi-
ately after his birth as son of Devakī and Vasu-deva
was entrusted to her care, that he might be protected
from the enmity of Kaṃsa); N. of the wife of
Mahā-vīra and daughter of Samara-vīra; N. of the
daughter of a class of Manes.
—यशो-दत्त, अस्, m.
a proper N.
—यशो-दा, आस्, आस्, अम्, Ved. glory-
giving, conferring beauty, (for यशो-दा, f. of यशो-
द, see above.)
—यशोदा-गर्भ-सम्भूता, f.
epithet of Durgā.
—यशोदा-नन्द, अस्, m. Yaśo-
dā's son, i. e. Kṛṣṇa.
—यशो-देव, अस्, m., N. of
[]
a Buddhist mendicant; of a son of Rāma-candra;
(ई), f., N. of a daughter of Vainateya and wife of
Bṛhan-manas.
—यशो-धन, अम्, n. a fund or
stock of fame; (अस्, आ, अम्), whose wealth consists
of fame, rich in renown, renowned, famous (said of
persons); (अस्), m., N. of a king.
—यशो-धर,
अस्, आ, अम्, maintaining or preserving glory, uphold-
ing renown; (अस्), m., N. of the fifth day of the
civil month (कर्म-मास); of the eighteenth
Arhat of the preceding and of the nineteenth of the
future Utsarpiṇī; of a son of Kṛṣṇa by Rukmiṇī,
(also read यशो-वर); of various other men; (आ),
f., N. of the fourth night of the civil month; of the
mother of Rāhula; of several other women.
—यशो-
धा, आस्, आस्, अम्, conferring splendor or fame.
—यशो-धामन्, अ, n. site or abode of glory.
—यशो-नन्दि, इस्, m., N. of a king.
—यशो-भ-
गिन्, ई, इनी, इ, Ved. possessing fame, rich in glory,
famous, renowned.
—यशो-भगीन, अस्, आ, अम्, or
यशो-भग्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved., see Pāṇ. IV. 4, 131.
—यशो-भद्र, अस्, m. (with Jainas) N. of one of
the six Śruta-kevalins.
—यशो-भृत्, त्, त्, त्, bearing
fame, possessing renown, famous, renowned; bring-
ing glory.
—यशो-मती, f., N. of the third lunar
night.
—यशो-मत्य, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people.
—यशो-माधव, अस्, m. a form of Viṣṇu.
—य-
शो-मित्र, अस्, m., N. of a Buddhist author.
—यशो-
राज, अस्, m. a proper N.
—यशो-राशि, इस्, m. a
heap or mass of glory, a glorious deed.
—यशो-
लेखा f., N. of a princess.
—यशो-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्,
possessing fame or glory; (अती), f., N. of various
women; of a district (originally of a stream; some-
times abbreviated into यशो-वति); of a mythical
town on mount Meru.
—यशो-वर, अस्, m., N. of
a son of Kṛṣṇa by Rukmiṇī, (see यशो-धर.)
—यशो-वर्त्मन्, अ, n. the path of glory, road to
fame.
—यशो-वर्मन्, आ, m., N. of a poet; of
several other men, (यशो-वर्मक is found at the
end of an adj. comp.)
—यशो-हन्, आ, घ्नी, अ, de-
stroying fame or reputation.
—यशो-हर, अस्, आ,
अम्, taking away fame, depriving of reputation,
dishonouring; N. of a place, (gender doubtful.)
—यशोहर-जित्, त्, m., N. of Kacu-rāya.
—यशो-
हीन, अस्, आ, अम्, shorn of fame or glory.
यशस at the end of a comp. = यशस्.

यशस्य, अस्, आ, अम्, famous, glorious, renowned,
celebrated, honoured; bestowing glory or distinction,
producing fame, creditable; (आ), f., N. of a plant (=
जीवन्ती); of another plant (= ऋद्धि).
यशस्यु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. seeking favour.

यष्टिक, अस्, m. a species of water-fowl (= जल-
कुक्कुट; cf. को-यष्टि); a bird, the lapwing;
(आ), f. a staff, stick, club; a particular pearl ornament
or necklace (especially of one string); an oblong
pond or tank; liquorice.
यष्टीक, अम्, n. liquorice (= यष्टि-मधु).

यष्ट्रस्क यष्ट्रस्क (?), आस्, m. pl., N. of a
people.

यस् यस् (probably connected with rt.
यम्), cl. 4. 1. P. यस्यति, यसति, य-
यास, यसितुम्, to froth up, foam (Ved.; but ac-
cording to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda VII. 104, 2, ययस्तु
= आयासम् प्राप्नोतु = उपक्षीयताम्), to make
great effort or exertion, strive, endeavour, labour,
preserve, trouble one's self; to strive after (with
dat.); [cf. Gr. ζέ-ω, (ζέν-νυμι, ἔ-ζεσ-μαι, ζέσ-σε-ν),
ζέα-μα, ζέ-μα, ζέ-σι-ς, ζεσ-τό-ς, ζῆ-λο-ς; Old
Germ. jes-an, ger-ja-n.]

यसित्वा or यस्त्वा, ind. making effort, endeavour-
ing.

यस्क, अस्, m. a proper N.; (आस्), m. pl. the de-
scendants of Yaska; यस्का गैरिक्षिताः, N. of a
school.

यास्क यास्क, अस्, m. (fr. यस्क), a patro-
[]
nymic, N. of the author of the Nirukta or commen-
tary on the difficult Vedic words contained in the
lists called Nighaṇṭus, (these consist of three divisions,
1. the Naighaṇṭuka or a list of synonymous words,
2. the Naigama or words usually occurring in the
Veda only, 3. the Daivata or words relating to deities
and sacrificial acts; according to some, these three
lists were drawn up by Yāska himself, and then com-
mented on in his Nirukta, which quotes Vedic pas-
sages in illustration of the words, and is the oldest
Vedic commentary extant; Yāska is supposed to
have lived before Pāṇini); (आस्), m. pl. the pupils of
Yaska.

यस्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be endeavoured, to be done
with energy or perseverance; (according to a com-
mentator) = वध्य, to be killed, fit or ready for
slaughter.
—यस्य-त्व, अम्, n. effort, energy; fit-
ness for slaughter; death.

यास्यत्, अन्, अती or अन्ती, अत्, about to go, about
to proceed.

याशु याशु, n. (perhaps connected with rt.
यस्), embracing, embrace, sexual union, (according
to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda 1. 126, 6. याशूनि = प्रजनन-
सम्बन्धीनि कर्माणि = भोगाः.)

याशोधरेय याशोधरेय (fr. यशो-धरा),
अस्, m. a metronymic of Rāhula (the son of Śākya-
muni).

याशोभद्र याशोभद्र (fr. यशो-भद्र), अस्,
m., N. of the fourth day of the civil month (कर्म-
मास).
यास्कायनि, इस्, m. a patronymic from Yāska.

यास्कायनीय or यास्कीय, आस्, m. pl. the pupils
of Yāskāyani.
